Auditable Arbitration for Resolution

When an answer is not wrong, but the reason is gone.

A2R measures and reduces source-resolution distortion in LLM output arbitration: the irreversible loss or incorrect mapping of task-relevant source structure when several candidate answers become one.

01 / About

A reasonable synthesis can still erase the decision.

The paper starts with a concrete multi-agent question, not with a metric: Can a U.S. AI medical-record product enter the Chinese market directly?

The point is not whether the final sentence sounds fluent. It is whether the source-side relation that made the decision meaningful remains recoverable after arbitration.

01 / QUERY

One question, two candidate resolutions.

Multiple agents investigate the same market-entry decision and return answers that carry different kinds of structure.

02 / CANDIDATE A

“Market, procurement, and technical checks can proceed in parallel.”

parallel checks
03 / CANDIDATE B

“Product classification must precede selection of the regulatory pathway.”

prerequisite relation
04 / ARBITRATION

“Conduct all investigations in parallel while continuing to confirm the regulatory classification.”

sounds reasonable
WHAT CHANGED?

A prerequisite became a process reminder.

The arbitration result is not plainly false. But it no longer preserves the dependency that product classification determines the regulatory pathway. The two ideas are mentioned; the relation between them has been aliased.

03Final answerrelation lost

A2R calls this source-resolution distortion: the irreversible loss or incorrect mapping of task-relevant source-side structure during arbitration.

THE RESEARCH QUESTION

When an LLM compresses multiple candidate outputs into one result, how can we measure the distortion of task-relevant source structure - and how can we reduce it?

That question motivates both the source-bounded measurement framework and the A2R method below.
02 / Method

Protect the resolution structure before compressing the answer.

A2R-Decision changes the object that the final generator is allowed to rewrite. It does not ask an LLM to remember a hidden checklist; it makes the local resolution state explicit, then renders only claims authorized by that state.

In the pairwise setting, the resolver maps a query and two candidate outputs to a compact result. The method separates extraction, local resolution, and final rendering so each source of distortion can be inspected.

PAIRWISE UNIT OF ANALYSIS

Arbitration is a compression map.

For x = (q, A, B), the system must decide which source units matter, how they relate under the query, and what the final answer is licensed to claim. The same framework extends to three candidates by adding UC.

F(q, A, B)→(ŷ, L̂)

A2R keeps an optional ledger L̂ instead of collapsing every decision directly into free-form text.

QUERY-CONDITIONED REFERENCE
Sq(x) = (UA, UB, Eq, Pq, Qq)
  • UA, UB - query-relevant source units
  • Eq - relations between units under the query
  • Pq - provenance that must remain recoverable
  • Qq - caveats and the claims they qualify
Stage 1 / ExtractE

Query-relevant source units

Read the query and candidate answers, then keep content that may license a final claim: a local claim, evidence statement, recommendation, caveat, constraint, or risk note.

uᵢ = (idᵢ, sourceᵢ, textᵢ,
typeᵢ, flagsᵢ)
preserve source ID · original span · function flags
Stage 2 / ResolveL

Compact decision ledger

For each local judgment, record the units involved, their query-conditioned relation, the licensed claim, the resolution operation, and its provenance category.

ℓₘ = (dₘ, Iₘ, rₘ, oₘ,
cₘ, pₘ)
decision ID · units · relation · operation · claim · provenance
Stage 3 / RenderG

Ledger-constrained rendering

Generate from the ledger with a deterministic template: order claims, merge adjacent entries on the same topic, add connectives, and inherit caveat scope and provenance.

ŷ = G(L̂)
organize · render · attach recoverable tags
(q, A, B)→Û→L̂→ŷ extract · resolve · constrained generate
mergeEquivalent or additive

Combine compatible units without erasing their source roles.

condition_sourcesIncompatible but conditioned

Keep conditional alternatives when different conclusions are licensed under identifiable conditions.

dropQuery-invalid

Do not authorize a final claim from a unit that does not answer the query.

report_unresolvedNo decision criterion

State the alternatives and the missing criterion instead of forcing a choice.

WHY THE LEDGER MATTERS

The opening example rendered from an authorized decision.

The ledger records Candidate A and Candidate B under one decision record, while preserving the prerequisite scope from Candidate B. The final text can be concise without turning a dependency into a vague reminder.

[r1][resolution] For non-regulatory matters,
market, procurement, and technical research can
proceed in parallel following Candidate A; given
the prerequisite specified by Candidate B, investigation
of the regulatory pathway should begin after product
classification is determined.
THE DESIGN PRINCIPLE

Anti-aliasing protects distinguishable signal components before irreversible downsampling. A2R applies the same ordering intuition to arbitration: preserve the source units and local relations first, then perform the tighter final aggregation.

03 / Evidence

Measure what survives, not just what sounds good.

The gold source structure is fixed before system execution. Evaluation then asks where the structure is lost: during extraction, in the ledger, or while rendering the final answer.

Final-only and final-plus-trace outputs are scored separately. The framework evaluates source recoverability, not the external truth of the candidate content.

01 / DE

Extraction

Were the query-relevant units retained from the candidate set?

02 / DL

Ledger

Did relations, provenance assignments, and caveat attachments remain explicit?

03 / DR

Rendering

Did the final claims preserve the authorized structure and source links?

Six observable distortion signals.

The primary metrics are CER and Prov-H. FCR, UAR, and CPR act as safety diagnostics; RF* is reserved for mechanism analysis because relation labels are harder to annotate reliably.

CERconflict erasure
FCRfalse conflict
UARunsupported addition
Prov-Hprovenance exposure + correctness
CPRcaveat preservation
RF*query-conditioned relation fidelity
Final-only fidelity↓ lower is better · ↑ higher is better

05 / Dataset

A benchmark for source-bounded arbitration.

The benchmark fixes gold source structures before system execution, so evaluation can focus on what arbitration preserved, erased, or mapped incorrectly.

Open dataset
320controlled diagnostic cases
200natural pairwise cases
